newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian T-bond tender uncertain this week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian T-bond tender uncertain this week.

text.p: A fixed-rate Australian Treasury bond tender is possible this week although the market's gyrations of the past few days may see the Treasury hold fire, traders said.
"The rumour in the market is that (the tender) will be in the April 2000 and the September 2009 (stocks)," said one trader at a European bank based in Sydney.
The surprise announcement on Friday of a A$300 million Treasury adjustable rate bonds (TABs) tender for today, a day earlier than usual, fuelled expectations of a fixed rate bond offering this week.
If a tender does go ahead, details would be announced at 12.00 p.m. (0100 GMT) with final bids due on Tuesday.
"I personally think there will be a tender, but there are a lot of people who don't," said one trader at a local bank, who say the Treasury tapping the January 2001 bonds along with the 2009 issue.
A tender announcement would fit in with the issuance timetable outlined by Tony Hinton, First Assistant Secretary, Investment and Debt Division Commwealth Treasury, in early November.
He said then there would be two fixed rate tenders and one TABS tender before the end of the year.

The market has already had one of the fixed rate tenders on November 19, and the feeling is the Treasury would prefer to get the other one away before the market starts winding down for the year-end holidays.

However, given the volatile price action over the past few days, which saw long-dated yield jump 40 basis points at one stage on Friday amid the market's largest one-day sell-off since March, it may see the Treasury hold back this week, traders added. -- Colin Brinsden 61-2 9373-1800
